Specification: Keep observed arrival/departure timestamps immutable; create separate simulated timestamp columns.
Within each IMO_Normalised, sort by Actual_Arrival_UTC then Simulation_Record_ID; flag same-time ties and overlapping calls for review.
Caveat: Observed sequence is not proof of physical route.

Specification: For consecutive calls, calculate next observed arrival minus current observed departure.
Caveat: Elapsed time includes unobserved components; not pure sailing time.

Specification: Apply an explicitly approved shock to a defined call, transition, port service, or access condition.
Caveat: No affected scope or magnitude currently approved.

Specification: For each vessel in sequence, calculate simulated arrival as the later of baseline arrival plus direct shock and previous simulated departure plus the specified inter-call elapsed-time treatment.
Caveat: Requires a defensible transition-time treatment; observed elapsed time is not automatically sailing time.

Specification: If the experiment is a pure schedule displacement, shift arrival and departure equally; if service disruption changes stay, define a separate service-time mechanism.
Caveat: Do not combine displacement and service-duration change implicitly.

Specification: Recovery may alter only explicitly defined simulated timing or decision variables; log action, magnitude, feasibility and affected vessel/call.
Caveat: No recovery policy selected by this specification.

Specification: Mark calls/vessels whose downstream sequence extends beyond the observation/simulation horizon; report unrecovered and censored separately.
Caveat: Avoid treating right-censored outcomes as recovered.

Specification: Report call-level and vessel-level accumulated/final delay separately; distinguish maximum final vessel delay from maximum accumulated delay per vessel.
Caveat: Do not mix call sums with unique-vessel measures.

Specification: Check chronological order, non-negative durations, no unintended overlaps, event balance, reproducibility, baseline invariance and explicit scope traceability.
